..
Weak trade wind showers are making their way over the Marianas this
afternoon. Moisture is expected to stay high enough for this pattern
to continue for much of the week. Winds should be light enough for 
island effect showers to develop over the west side of Guam from Apra
Harbor south to Malesso, so scattered showers are in the forecast 
for that area. Scattered showers are expected for all the Marianas by
Wednesday due to further weakening of the winds and potentially 
increased moisture from a trade wind trough moving through. Island
effect showers may continue through the end of the week if moisture 
is sufficient enough.

Marine...
Models, coastal buoys, SOFAR buoys, and spotter observations 
indicate that surf is high enough to induce a moderate risk of rip 
currents along east facing reefs of the Marianas through Wednesday 
and north and west facing reefs through at least tonight. Combined 
seas of 3 to 5 feet will persist through at least Monday night 
before starting to slowly decrease. The dominant swells are the 
easterly trade wind swell and the westerly swell from distant 
Typhoon Jangmi. Winds are decreasing to light to gentle tonight, 
potentially becoming light by Tuesday night.

Eastern Micronesia...
Latest satellite imagery shows cloudy skies with numerous showers 
and isolated thunderstorms over Kosrae, and mostly cloudy skies with
scattered showers to the southeast of Pohnpei. At Majuro, isolated
showers are present with increasing clouds and convection over the
last couple of hours. Altimetry shows seas between 2 and 4 feet for
Pohnpei and Kosrae and 3 to 5 feet for Majuro.

Model guidance is having a difficult time with the Near-Equatorial
Trough (NET). Latest satellite trends show the NET is now farther
north than previously expected. Therefore, convection has increased
across Kosrae, with numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms over
the island and waters. This looks to continue through tonight while
convection increases westward into Pohnpei. Maintained POPs
(Probability of Precipitation) in the scattered range of 30 to 50
percent through the week for Pohnpei, with the same for Kosrae
beginning Tuesday morning. This is due to the NET remaining over the
region with weak trade-wind troughs moving through and interacting
with the NET. Overall, the pattern looks to be a bit more wet than
the previous forecast. For Majuro, isolated showers prevail over the
Marshalls for now. However, increasing convergence along a weak
southwest to northeast oriented trough is increasing and satellite
trends show increasing convection across Majuro. Majuro looks to
remain on the eastern end of the main convection and can expect POPs
to fluctuate between 20 and 30 percent into the weekend.

No changes to the marine forecast. Fairly benign conditions are 
expected to continue through the remainder of the week into the 
weekend. Mostly light to gentle winds with seas between 2 and 4 feet 
for Pohnpei and Kosrae and between 4 and 5 feet for Majuro.

Western Micronesia... 
A near-equatorial trough (NET) extends between Palau and Yap Proper
to a broad disturbance in southeastern Yap State near 4N146E, then
curves northeastward to pass south of Chuuk Lagoon. An area of
scattered showers have pushed southwest of Yap Proper due to a 
slight southward shift in the NET, with CIMSS MIMIC precipitable 
water imagery showing relatively drier air of 1.7 inches beginning to
move over Yap Proper this afternoon. Mainly isolated showers are 
expected tonight through Thursday for Yap. Isolated to scattered 
showers linger across Palau through at least Tuesday afternoon due 
to the proximity of the NET axis and relatively moist 
southwesterlies. The NET disturbance looks to drift northwest through
Yap State, possibly weakening around midweek, however, this may 
still promote spotty showers near Yap and Palau through late week. A 
portion of the NET remains fairly active near Chuuk this week, with 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms continuing through much 
of the week, with a peak in numerous showers on Wednesday.

Benign marine conditions are expected this week. Altimetry data 
shows seas around 4 to 5 feet. As northwest and west-southwest 
swells continue to diminish, combined seas are expected to subside to
3 to 4 feet. Light to gentle winds become light and variable for 
Palau and Chuuk starting Tuesday and light easterly winds are 
expected for Yap starting Tuesday night.
